deviations.what: The line replaces every NA new_classes with 0, so a firm-year with an empty base gets 0 instead of the required NA.
new_classes is computed from the forward set without checking whether the base is empty, so a firm-year with an empty base and a non-empty forward set gets |F| instead of NA.

notes: The rest of the code matches the spec: filing-year dating, first-listed class with missing classes dropped, base window k=1..5 and forward window k=1..3 with year t excluded, the anti-join for new classes, de-duplication, and one output row per firm_year pair. The code treats an empty-string subclass as missing and leaves the 1987-2015 focal years to the firm_year input; the spec is silent on the first and lists the second only as a setting, so I did not count either as a deviation.
